chapter_theme: Last songs at Thiruchendur (திருச்செந்தூர், 6 of 6): the poet asks for Murugan's feet at the hour of death and at the fading of house, wife and child, confesses his capture by women's eyes and his voyages abroad for money to win them, and traces his body from seed through many burnings; one song speaks for a lovesick girl of the hills. The praise turns on Brahma imprisoned, the vel against Sura and the hill, Siva who drank the poison, and the shore of Alaivay and Senthil.
structure_note: All eight end at Senthil or Alaivay. 96 and 97 set the plea at life's end (Death's coming; the fading of child, house and wife); 98, 99, 102 and 103 confess women; 100 asks for release from births in Saiva terms; 101 is in another voice, for a girl sick with love.

96.reading: The poet pictures his death: women who think many things in one deceitful heart, the sons and the kin gathered at evening crowd round wailing, the worm-like body wrapped in cloth goes to be food for the fire, and victorious Yama comes near to terrify; on that day, he asks, give your pair of feet. The praise names the peacock hero who made lotus-born Brahma suffer and imprisoned him, the chest that the sweet-voiced lady embraces, Senthil where poets of fine speech weigh the Tamil of the Sangam, and the one who fought so that the golden northern mountain scattered into the sea.
96.nuance: The plea is the pilot's hour-of-death formula: அண்டிப் பயமுற வென்றிச் சமன் வரும் அன்றைக்கு அடியிணை தரவேணும். The wailing wife, sons and kin (மடவார், புதல்வர், கிளைஞர்) are the household that cannot help at death, and the body is பஞ்சிப் புழுவுடல் அங்கிக்கு இரை, a worm-body for the fire. Brahma's imprisonment appears without the Om teaching. The line on the chest (கண்டொத்த அனமொழி அண்டத் திருமயில் கண்டத்து அழகிய) is hard to split; 'a woman with speech like sugar candy' is the likely sense.

97.reading: The poet names what a man holds to, the baby that crawls up again and again crying for him, the house of golden halls that seem to split the sky, the wife with curled hair and kumkum on her breasts taken as refuge, and asks for Murugan's lotus feet with their anklets and kadamba at the time when these fade. The praise names Senthil of sandal, mandara, sugarcane and plantain, Murugan who crossed the cool forest into the millet field and bowed to the girl with sweet words, and the lord whom Siva, Indra and the gods trust.
97.nuance: மங்கு காலம், the time of fading, is the key: the child, the house and the wife are listed with delight before the turn. The song is set in very short rhythmic units, so many words are split; the last six lines (அந்தகன் கலங்க வந்த ... கும்பர் நம்பு தம்பிரானே) can be divided more than one way, and I have given only their outline.

98.reading: A short song: the poet asks that he not waste away morning and evening in the bond of desire for dark-eyed women and for children, and that Murugan give him love for his two feet. The praise names him the protector, the son of Parameswara's grace and the nephew of Hari Kesava, at Alaivay.
98.nuance: மடமாதர் மக ஆசை தொந்தம்: the bond (தொந்தம்) joins desire for women and for children in one phrase. The plea is not for release but for love (இருதாளின் அன்பு).

99.reading: The poet speaks of women whose eyes press like fate and whose foreheads are like the moon, who join young men's minds, offer pleasure to drink its fill and say 'rule us sweetly', and asks whether the dark sorrow and delusion of maya that come to tear him will never end. The praise names Siva who wears the moon, drank the rising poison so the gods might live, rides the bull and comes to the side of devotees who never forget, and Murugan his son, who fought the Suras of great sorcery with the vel, on the peacock at Alaivay.
99.nuance: விதிபோலும் உந்த விழி makes the women's eyes press on a man like fate. மருள் மாயை, delusion and maya, names the poet's condition in doctrinal terms, and the Suras who are defeated are themselves அதிமாயம், great maya, so the praise answers the plea.

100.reading: The poet says his body came from seed and has burned a crore of times, and asks that from now on, like the knowing ones who never part from Murugan's feet, he too may have his ruin and old sin ended, take the form of Siva-knowledge, rise to the strong state and rest, and be given the flower feet. The praise names Siva, the one red flame within the poet, with fire in his eye and flame-coloured hair, helper of devotees, and Murugan his son, who embraces the beautiful hunter girl of wisdom, at Senthil.
100.nuance: விந்ததின் ஊறி வந்தது காயம் வெந்தது கோடி: the body comes from seed and has been burned on the pyre countless times, so the plea is against rebirth itself. சிவஞான வடிவு and எந்தன் உளே ஏக செஞ்சுடர் give the song a Saiva Siddhanta cast. விஞ்சையர் may be the Vidyadharas or simply the wise; ஞானம் என் குறமாது makes Valli herself wisdom.

101.reading: Spoken for a girl of the hunters' hill who is sick with love: Kama's five flower arrows scatter, the moon burns like the sun, the soft breeze comes like fire and spiteful women speak blame, and the speaker asks Murugan to come near with his cool garland to end her cruel infatuation. The praise names him the wise one whom Siva, holder of the leaping deer, worshipped with joy, the hero who threw the vel so that the hill and the mango scattered and the sea feared, and the one who removes the troubles of devotees, at Alaivay.
101.nuance: This is an akam song: குறவாணர் குன்றில் உறை பேதை is spoken of in the third person, by her mother or friend, and the cure asked is Murugan's garland, the lover's token. The moon, breeze and gossip (வினைமாதர் தம்தம் வசைகூற) are the stock torments of the separated woman. மறிமான் உகந்த இறையோன் ... வழிபாடு தந்த makes Siva the worshipper of his son.

102.reading: The poet says that taking women's eyes for cruel black arrows and fish, their speech for cuckoos' song and their hair as soft as it seems, he went seeking wealth as far as Bengal, Sonam and China to join their soft shoulders, and asks whether he must suffer such hard pain; he asks the strong-shouldered young lord to come and rule him at this hour. The praise names Murugan sweet to the hill girl, who fought in anger so that the hill, the seas and Sura were lost, and the son of Siva who bears the skeleton, lord of the gods, at Senthil.
102.nuance: பொருள்தேடி வங்காளம் சோனம் சீனம் போய்: the price of women is paid with wealth earned by voyages to distant lands, a merchant's confession rather than a poet's. சோனம் is not certain (perhaps a land to the east). The song is set in heavy monosyllabic beats (வெங்காளம் பாணம் சேல் கண்), so the splits are not all sure.

103.reading: The poet asks of a woman's eye whether it is a fierce lotus, harsh poison, a fish, a sea of pleasure, a slice of mango, the arrow of the burnt Kama that defeated Siva, a dark flower, a refuge or the heart of Yama's messengers, and, sunk in such women's breasts and in doubt, asks whether a day will come when Murugan gives his feet with their anklets and garlands. The praise names the vel that turned Taraka of the five great sins to ash, let the gods return to Amaravati as before and told Brahma and Vishnu not to fear, and Murugan as the treasure of Siva who wears Ganga, flowers and the moon in his matted hair, at Senthil.
103.nuance: The opening is a chain of doubting comparisons (ஓ ... ஓ ...), ending with தஞ்சமோ யமதூதுவர் நெஞ்சமோ: is the eye a refuge or Death's servants' heart? The poet's own state is சங்கை, doubt. Kama the enemy of Sambara (சம்பராரி) is said to have defeated Siva before he was burnt.

links.note: Both put a woman's eye to a doubting question with Death among the answers. The Kural asks whether it is Death, an eye or a doe and finds all three; 103 lengthens the list to poison, fish, Kama's arrow and Yama's messengers, and turns the doubt into the poet's own confusion before he asks for Murugan's feet.

source_issues: Song 100: one corrupt character in விந்ததினு஡றி (line 1); clearly விந்ததின் ஊறி.
Song 103: சுழ்தரு (line 15) should be சூழ்தரு; not flagged as corrupt.
